extracted.intended_audience: talented early-career scientists considering applying for an ERC Starting Grant
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Starting Grant proposal, plus the evaluation criteria and administrative/host-institution requirements. Targets early-career researchers seeking independent funding to lead a research project in EU/Associated countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — years since PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD (Extensions are possible under certain circumstances — see the latest ERC Work Programme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core eligibility rule for the Starting Grant; check the ERC Work Programme for permitted extensions (e.g. career breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant profile — track record and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A talented early-career scientist who has already produced excellent supervised work, is ready to work independently and shows potential to be a research leader; a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI is evaluated on their track record and potential to lead; readiness to work independently and leadership potential are expected attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible proposals — any field and bottom-up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no thematic priorities — submit proposals across any discipline covered by the ERC panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution (HI) — location and type requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a Host Institution/HI) located in one of the EU Member States or the Associated Countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HI can be where the applicant already works or another HI in EU/Associated countries; the legal hosting entity must be based in an eligible country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution legal and contractual role
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant must be submitted by a single Principal Investigator (PI) in conjunction with and on behalf of their Host Institution, called the applicant legal entity. Grants are awarded to the Host Institution with the explicit commitment that this institution offers appropriate conditions for the Principal Investigator independently to direct the research and manage its funding for the duration of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HI must formally commit to support PI independence in directing the research and managing funds; the HI is the legal grantee even though the PI leads the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted host institution types
rubrics_metrics.description: Any type of legal entity, including universities, research centres and undertakings can host the PI and his/her team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legally the host institution must be based in an EU Member State or an associated country.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI location at submission and required agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI does not necessarily need to be working at the host institution at the time when the proposal is submitted. However, a mutual agreement and the host institution’s commitment on how the relationship will be established are necessary, should the proposal be successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not already employed by the HI, secure a formal mutual agreement and commitment from the HI in advance or be prepared to provide it upon grant award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams may include non-European members; vacancies for team members can be published on Euraxess-Jobs; implementing arrangements exist to host non-European scientists in Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum funding and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project budgets and timelines around the standard maximum of €1.5M/5 years unless prorated for shorter projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional budget allowance (start-up/equipment/facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional €0.5 million can be made available to cover eligible 'start-up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include justified requests for the extra €0.5M for start-up, major equipment or large facility access — these are conditional and eligible only under the specified reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost coverage and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetaries should separate eligible direct costs and the 25% flat-rate contribution for indirect costs according to ERC rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanism — Calls for Proposals and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal should be submitted by the specified closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit in response to an open call; ensure administrative forms, proposal text and all required supplementary documents are included before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call publication channels and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls are published on this page, the European Commission’s Participant Portal and in the Official Journal of the European Union. The ERC has yearly calls for proposals covering all scientific fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor these official channels for call openings and deadlines; calls are annual and cover all fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission planning steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: Find out which ERC grant and which call is suitable for you. Identify the host institution and team members you would like to work with. Contact the National Contact Point (NCP) in your country for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early identification of HI, team and contact with NCP improves preparedness and increases likelihood of a complete, competitive application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and submission best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the call is open: Read the call documents carefully. Contact the host institution and gather all the details you need for the application. Start writing your proposal. Allow time for other people to review your draft. Familiarise yourself with the Participant Portal’s submission service. Submit your proposal as early as possible. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by simply submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one. You will get an ‘acknowledgement of receipt’ by e-mail for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for internal review and feedback (NCP, peers); practice using the submission portal; submit early and overwrite if needed before the deadline; keep the acknowledgement email as proof of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility check and external evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline: The ERC will check whether your proposal meets the call’s eligibility criteria. External experts will evaluate all the eligible proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting formal eligibility is necessary to proceed to peer review; expect external peer review by independent experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole evaluation criterion — excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both project excellence and PI excellence are jointly considered — craft both the scientific case and the PI's track-record/vision to demonstrate excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, quality threshold and ranking (funding selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are in charge of assessing and scoring the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieving a score above the quality threshold is necessary but not sufficient — success depends on ranking relative to other proposals and available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel structure and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 25 panels, each covering a sub-section of one of three domains: Social Sciences and Humanities (SH), Life Sciences (LS), Physical and Engineering Sciences (PE). Each ERC panel consists of a chairman and 10-16 members. The Panel Chair and the Panel Members are selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of their scientific reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the most appropriate panel/sub-panel for your proposal and be aware panels are staffed by senior scientists selected for reputation; paneling affects evaluation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of remote experts (referees)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the Panel Members (who act as 'generalists'), the ERC evaluations rely on input from remote experts external to the panel, called referees. They are scientists and scholars who bring in the necessary specialised expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect both panel-level generalist assessment and specialist referee reports; ensure specialised technical aspects are clearly presented to be understandable by both audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency on panel chairs and members publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the deadline of a call, the names of the Panel Chairs are published on the ERC website. Similarly, the names of Panel Members are published, however, after the evaluation process is concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel chair identities are public before the deadline (useful for understanding panel expertise); panel member names are disclosed only after evaluation completes.
